payload.name: Extract All Explicitly Stated Memory Details
payload.description: When a user reflectively recounts a past experience and explicitly mentions multiple distinct details (activities, places, topics shared, outcomes), during extraction.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly lists several distinct details about one past experience (for example, activities, routes, topics discussed, or emotional outcomes), include every explicitly stated detail in the candidate; do not summarize only the main gist.
If the details form a bounded list in one statement, one candidate is enough; do not create separate candidates for each detail or add unmentioned details.
During CRUD, if a later message supplies an omitted explicit detail for an existing memory, UPDATE or MERGE that memory to add the detail instead of creating a duplicate.

candidates.solves: When a user recounts a past experience and explicitly lists multiple concrete details (activities, routes, topics shared, outcomes), extraction may keep only the main gist and drop one of the explicitly stated details, leaving the stored memory incomplete.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Focus Statements
payload.description: When a user explicitly states what they are currently focusing on, prioritizing, or spending time on, during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit statement of current focus, priority, or emphasis (e.g., 'I've been focusing on X', 'I'm prioritizing Y'), create a candidate memory capturing the stated focus, including the activity or relationship involved.
Use memory kind 'state' for ongoing focus or 'relationship' when the focus is on a person/relationship; record temporal markers like 'lately' or 'currently' when stated.
During CRUD, when updating an existing memory about the same subject, preserve or merge the explicit focus fact; do not let a new activity detail replace the focus statement.
Stop after capturing the focus in one memory per subject per time period; do not add duplicate memories for examples that merely illustrate the focus.

candidates.solves: When a user explicitly describes what they are currently focusing on or prioritizing, the construction pipeline often captures illustrative activities but drops the explicit focus statement, so later queries about focus fail. This skill instructs extraction and update to preserve explicit focus/priority statements as durable memories.

payload.name: Preserve All Explicitly Enumerated Items in Memories
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists multiple activities, preferences, or attributes for the same subject and you are extracting or updating a memory, include every listed item.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly enumerates multiple activities, preferences, or attributes for the same subject (e.g., 'loves A, B, and C'), create one candidate whose content includes every explicitly listed item; do not drop any item during summarization.

During CRUD, when merging or updating an existing memory for the same subject, preserve all previously stored enumerated items and add any new explicitly listed items; do not replace a full list with a partial one.

Stop once all explicitly stated items are captured; do not add unmentioned activities or details, and do not split the list into multiple duplicate memories unless the items describe distinct memory kinds.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes compress a message that enumerates several explicit activities or preferences into a memory containing only a subset, causing later questions about omitted items to fail. This skill ensures that when a source explicitly lists multiple items for the same subject, the extracted or updated memory retains every listed item, while still avoiding invented details.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Media Evaluations
payload.description: When a user gives a first-person evaluative description of a specific movie, show, book, game, or other media item, extract the item and its stated qualities into memory.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a first-person evaluation of a specific media item (movie, show, book, game, etc.) with explicit descriptive words, create one durable preference or event memory capturing the item, the speaker, and the exact evaluative descriptors.
Use the user's own quality words (e.g., gripping, great actors) rather than a generic summary like 'liked it'.
Do not infer qualities that were not stated, and create at most one candidate per distinct media item mentioned.

candidates.solves: Users often state evaluative opinions about media they watched, read, or played (e.g., 'the story was gripping', 'the actors were great'). These explicit subjective assessments are missed during extraction, so later questions about how the user described the media cannot be answered. This skill ensures such first-person media evaluations are captured as durable memories.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Recommendations
payload.description: Use when a message contains explicit advice, suggestion, or recommendation from one person to another about what they should do or keep doing.
content: During extraction, if a speaker gives explicit advice, suggestion, or recommendation to another person about what they should do or keep doing, create a memory candidate that records the advice.
Capture the advisor, the addressee, the recommended action, and any stated reason or goal; use the message/session timestamp as the time.
Prefer a durable event or state memory for the advice; do not fold it into a feeling or comfort-source memory.
Extract only explicitly stated advice; do not infer recommendations from questions or general statements, and stop after one candidate per advice.

candidates.solves: Construction often drops explicit advice given by one speaker to another in multi-party conversations, so later questions about what someone suggested cannot be answered. This skill ensures such recommendations are extracted as durable, source-linked memory candidates.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Recommendations and Stated Preferences
payload.description: When a participant explicitly recommends an item, activity, or experience, or states a preference or liking for one, in any conversation.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit recommendation or stated preference (e.g., 'X is awesome/great/calming', 'I recommend X', 'I love X'), create a preference memory for the speaker capturing the item and the stated evaluation or context.

Attribute the memory to the actual speaker (who made the recommendation), not the person asking; if the speaker recommends something for another person, record both the speaker's recommendation and any stated recipient only when explicit.
When the same message lists multiple distinct recommendations or preferences, create one candidate per distinct item; do not merge them into a single summary unless they share one context.

Do not require a direct question to precede the recommendation, and do not skip it because it appears in casual or reflective conversation. Stop after capturing the stated items; do not infer unmentioned preferences.

candidates.solves: Construction often fails to ingest explicit preference and recommendation statements because no guiding Skill tells the extractor to treat likes and recommendations as durable memories when they appear in casual exchanges. As a result, later questions about what someone recommended or preferred cannot be answered. This Skill closes that gap by making explicitly stated preferences and recommendations into preference memories attributed to the actual speaker, without requiring a direct question or formal phrasing.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Resulting Plans
payload.description: Use when one participant explicitly suggests or advises another to take a specific action, especially when the recipient responds to the advice.
content: During extraction, treat one speaker's concrete, actionable advice to another (e.g., a recommended fix, next step, or change in behavior) as a memory-worthy candidate.
Capture the advised action, the advisor, and the recipient in the candidate; do not omit the suggestion even when it appears in casual dialogue or as an interjection.

If the recipient agrees, thanks, or states intent to act on the advice, also create a plan memory for the recipient with the suggested action; otherwise store the advice as a relationship or event memory linking the advisor and recipient.
Stop after capturing the concrete advice and resulting plan; do not generate hypothetical alternatives or unrelated follow-ups.

candidates.solves: Construction frequently misses explicit advice or suggestions exchanged between speakers, leaving later questions about what was recommended unanswered. This adds a reusable rule to extract concrete suggestions and any resulting plan as durable memories, with source links.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Recommendations with Qualifiers
payload.description: When a message explicitly recommends a named item (game, book, movie, show, activity, etc.) with an evaluative qualifier such as calming, cute, awesome, or fun.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly recommends a named item (e.g., a game, book, movie, show, activity) and attaches an evaluative qualifier (calming, cute, awesome, fun, etc.), create a preference memory for the person making the recommendation, capturing the item name and the qualifier.
Treat the recommendation itself as sufficient evidence of preference; do not require phrases like 'I like' or 'my favorite'.
If the recommendation names a recipient or another person, include that relationship context in the memory content; otherwise store it as the speaker's preference.
Emit at most one memory per recommended item per message; stop once the item and qualifier are captured, and do not add extra searches or details.

candidates.solves: Construction sometimes fails to persist explicitly stated recommendations and the evaluative qualifiers that make them memorable, so later questions about what someone recommended or liked cannot be answered. This skill ensures such statements become durable preference memories.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Recurring Favorites and Habits
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly names an activity, dish, or item they do, make, or enjoy often or call a favorite.
content: During extraction, if a speaker states they do or make a specific activity, dish, or item 'a lot', 'often', or calls it 'one of my favorites', create a durable preference or event memory for that stated habit.
Include only explicitly stated details such as frequency, cooking method, or reason; do not infer unmentioned dishes or activities.
Do not skip the fact just because it is part of a casual reply or contains no direct question; the explicit statement is sufficient evidence.
Stop after capturing the named favorite and its stated context; do not enumerate every similar habit.

candidates.solves: Construction sometimes ignores explicit statements of a speaker's recurring or favorite activities (for example, a dish they often cook) when the statement appears in casual conversation, so no durable memory is created and later questions about that preference cannot be answered.

payload.name: Extract all components of multi-part advice
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists multiple distinct tips, strategies, or recommendations in one statement, extract every stated component into the candidate memory.
content: During extraction, if a message gives two or more distinct pieces of advice, strategies, or recommendations (e.g., connected by 'and', 'for', or listed as separate clauses), include every explicitly stated component in the candidate content.
Do not summarize the advice with only the first or most prominent item; each distinct component (e.g., breaking tasks, setting goals, using planners) must be represented.
Stop after the stated components are captured; do not add inferred advice or extra details.

candidates.solves: Extraction drops one or more components when a message presents an explicit multi-part tip, strategy, or recommendation. The stored memory captures only part of the stated advice, so later questions about the omitted component cannot be answered from memory.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Stated Preferences
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly names a favorite or preferred item (e.g., show, book, food, activity) in a message that also mentions shared interests or relationships.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly states a favorite or preferred item (e.g., "X is my favorite show"), create a profile or preference memory for that speaker containing the named item, even if the message also supports a broader relationship or shared-interest memory.
Do not let a generic relationship enrichment candidate absorb the specific preference; keep the explicit preference as its own candidate with the speaker as subject.
Create at most one candidate per explicitly named preference, and stop after the stated favorites are captured; do not infer additional favorites or expand to other topics.

candidates.solves: Extraction produces only a generic relationship or shared-interest memory and drops a speaker's explicitly stated favorite or preferred item, so later questions about that person's preferences cannot be answered. This skill ensures explicit preference statements are captured as standalone memories.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Advice Between Participants
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit suggestion, recommendation, or advice directed from one named person to another, capture it as a durable memory.
content: During extraction, if a speaker gives explicit advice, suggestion, or recommendation to another named participant (e.g., 'maybe look into X', 'you should try Y', 'consider Z'), create a candidate memory capturing the advisor, the advisee, the suggested action or option, and the topic or issue it addresses.
Prefer memory kind 'relationship' or 'event' as appropriate, and preserve directionality by recording who advised whom.
Do not require the advisee to accept or act on the advice; the suggestion itself is the fact to store.
Extract this even when the advice is embedded in conversational, polite, or hedged language or appears alongside unrelated topics.
Stop after capturing the advice; do not infer outcomes, reasons, or additional context not stated.

candidates.solves: Construction sometimes fails to store explicit advice exchanged between conversation participants, especially when phrased conversationally, so later questions about what one person suggested to another are unanswerable. This skill directs extraction of suggestion statements as relationship or event memories preserving the advisor, the advisee, and the recommended action.

payload.name: Extract explicit recommendations to named recipients
payload.description: When a message explicitly recommends specific items or activities (games, books, movies, restaurants, etc.) from one person to another, extract the recommendation as a memory.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly recommends specific items or activities to a named recipient (e.g., 'I recommend X', 'You should try Y', 'Z is great'), create a preference or relationship candidate with the recommender as subject and the recipient named in the content.
Capture the full list of recommended items; do not let an accompanying anecdote (e.g., how the speaker uses the item) replace the recommendation itself.
If the recommendation list spans multiple messages in the same conversational turn or nearby turns, consolidate all items into a single candidate.
Stop after capturing the recommendation; do not add searches or infer unmentioned recommended items.

candidates.solves: During memory extraction, explicit recommendations made by one person to another are often dropped or replaced by anecdotal details, so future questions about what was recommended cannot be answered. This skill ensures recommendations with their recipient and all listed items are captured as durable memory.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Suggestions and Recommendations
payload.description: Use when one speaker recommends, suggests, or tells another to check out, read, try, or use a specific item, resource, or activity.
content: During extraction, if a participant explicitly suggests or recommends that another participant check out, read, try, or use a specific item, resource, or activity, create a candidate memory capturing the suggestion.
Record the suggester, the recipient, the recommended item, and the stated purpose or benefit in the speaker's own words; do not require the recipient's acknowledgment or subsequent action.
Use an appropriate durable memory type (e.g., event or relationship) and link it to the source message; extract at most one memory per suggestion and stop after capturing the explicit recommendation.
During CRUD, process the suggestion candidate normally; do not skip or merge it solely because it is phrased as advice rather than a fact about the recipient.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes omit explicit recommendations or suggestions made by one participant to another, so later questions like 'What did X suggest Y check out?' cannot be answered from memory.

payload.name: Capture Complete Recommendation Lists
payload.description: When a speaker lists multiple recommendations, suggestions, or named items in one message or across consecutive turns during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message or consecutive messages from the same speaker present a set of recommendations, suggestions, or named items (e.g., introduced with 'a few', 'some', 'I recommend', or a numbered/bulleted list), create a memory candidate that includes every enumerated item.
Do not keep only the most detailed or last-mentioned item; capture all items together with their context, including the recommender and recipient if stated.
If items are spread across consecutive turns from the same speaker, combine them into a single candidate for that recommendation set.
Stop after capturing the explicit list; do not infer extra recommendations or search for additional items.

candidates.solves: When a speaker presents multiple recommendations, suggestions, or named items in one message or across consecutive turns, extraction often captures only the most detailed or last-mentioned item, causing later questions about the full set to fail. This skill ensures every explicitly listed item is preserved in memory.

payload.name: Capture Explicit Pet and Possession Names
payload.description: During extraction, when a speaker introduces a pet or owned item and states its proper name, include the name in the memory.
content: During extraction, when a speaker introduces or refers to a pet or owned item with an explicit proper name (e.g., 'This is [name]', 'my [item] [name]'), include that name in the ownership or relationship memory; do not store only the emotional or preference aspect.
If multiple named pets or items are mentioned, capture each stated name in the relevant memory so name-based queries are answerable.
During CRUD, when updating an existing pet or possession memory, preserve any recorded names; keep the memory compact and stop after recording owner, item type, and stated names.

candidates.solves: During extraction, the agent may record the emotional or general aspect of a statement (e.g., a pet brings comfort) while dropping explicitly stated proper names, so later questions asking for those names cannot be answered. This skill ensures that named identifying details are captured whenever a speaker introduces a pet or owned entity.

payload.name: Preserve Named Entities in Memories
payload.description: When a speaker names a pet, animal, or other entity during extraction, include the name(s) in the memory; capture each named instance individually.
content: During extraction, if a speaker names a pet, animal, or other personally owned/related entity (e.g., 'This is Susie', 'my second snake Seraphim'), include the name(s) in the memory content, even if the main point is emotional value or a story.
If multiple named instances of the same type are mentioned, capture each name (e.g., list both snake names) rather than summarizing the type only.
Select memory kind based on the relationship (e.g., 'relationship' for ownership, 'preference' for comfort) and stop after recording the named entity and its role; do not add extra searches.

candidates.solves: Prevents loss of specific names when creating memories from statements that emphasize emotional value or tell a story, so future queries about named pets or entities remain answerable.

payload.name: Extract Confirmed Accessory Use
payload.description: When a message states or confirms that the user puts clothing, accessories, or decorative items on a pet or owned object, during extraction.
content: During extraction, if the user explicitly says they dress, adorn, or put an item (hat, costume, bandana, etc.) on a pet or object they own, create a state or preference candidate capturing the subject and the item, even when the statement is framed as reassurance (e.g., 'it doesn't bother them, we put it on for fun').
Treat a habitual or repeated framing as sufficient; do not require a frequency adverb, but do not infer accessory use from a single past event unless it is described as recurring.
During CRUD, if an accessory-use memory already exists for the same subject and item, UPDATE or MERGE it; emit at most one candidate per distinct subject-item pair per message.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes misses durable facts about how a user dresses or accessorizes a pet or owned object, especially when the statement is framed as an answer to whether the item bothers them. This Skill ensures explicit confirmations of accessory use become state/preference memories so future questions about such habits can be answered.

payload.name: Extract Acquisition Source Separately
payload.description: When a user states how they acquired an item, pet, or possession, during extraction, even if the message also contains emotional or relationship statements.
content: During extraction, if a message states how the user obtained a pet, item, or possession (e.g., from a breeder, rescue, store, website, or another person), create a separate event memory recording the acquisition and its source.
Do not fold the acquisition source into a preference, relationship, or comfort-source memory; keep it as its own durable event so it survives later merges.

If an existing memory about the pet/item already exists, update or merge in the source when the later message explicitly provides it; stop after capturing the stated source and do not infer unmentioned acquisition details.

candidates.solves: When a user mentions both an emotional attachment to something (e.g., a pet) and the factual origin or acquisition source (e.g., breeder, rescue, store, website, person), extraction should preserve the factual source as its own memory instead of only capturing the emotional relationship.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Naming Rationale
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explains why a pet, object, or person was given a name, such as 'named after...' or 'I named it because...'.
content: During extraction, treat an explicit naming rationale as a distinct fact: capture the named entity, the namesake or reason, and the speaker who provided it.
If the named item already has a memory (e.g., a comfort source), add the naming-origin fact to that memory or create a separate event memory; do not replace or omit the stated rationale.
Record only what the speaker explicitly states about the name's origin and stop once the rationale is captured; do not infer unmentioned reasons.

candidates.solves: Extraction captures that an item exists but misses the speaker's explicit explanation of how or why it was named, leaving future name-origin questions unanswerable from memory.
